title: Low-level soluble chloride extraction in soil
author: Larsen, Waldron

steps.title: Homogenize and subsample soil
steps.instruction: Collect ~1 kg soil samples from the 8‑m borehole, homogenize in an industrial mixer to obtain a material of ~70 % sand and 30 % silt‑clay, then weigh 100 g subsamples for extraction analysis.

steps.title: Prepare extraction fluids
steps.instruction: Prepare the following extraction solutions: (a) deionized water with resistivity > 17.5 MΩ·cm for Method A; (b) 0.0001 M Na₂SO₄ solution for Method BL; (c) 0.001 M Na₂SO₄ solution for Method BH; (d) deionized water for Method C.

steps.title: Extract with Methods A, BL, BH
steps.instruction: For each of Methods A, BL, and BH use a 2:1 fluid‑to‑soil ratio (200 mL extraction fluid per 100 g soil) and perform three sequential rinses.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 mL of the appropriate extraction fluid to 100 g of homogenized soil in a suitable container.
Hand‑stir the mixture for 5 min.
Place the container on a mechanical shaker and shake for approximately 12 h.
Centrifuge the slurry at 3000 rpm for 45 min.
Collect the supernatant and pass it through a Whatman 40 ashless filter (filter chlorine content < 80 µg g⁻¹) to remove fine particles.
Repeat the entire sequence (add fresh fluid, stir, shake, centrifuge, filter) two more times on the same soil to obtain a total of three rinses.

steps.title: Extract with Method C
steps.instruction: Use a Nalgene 250 mL filter column fitted with an Osmonics 0.22 µm cellulosic filter and perform three sequential rinses, starting with a 1:1 fluid‑to‑soil ratio and ending with an overall 2:1 ratio.

substeps.instruction: Place 100 g of homogenized soil and 100 mL deionized water (1:1 ratio) into the column and seal it.
Apply nitrogen gas to the top of the column at 260 mm Hg to push the water through the soil.
Collect the filtrate and immediately re‑apply it to the top of the column for a second pass, thereby delivering a total of 200 mL fluid (overall 2:1 ratio).
Repeat the nitrogen‑push and collection steps two additional times to achieve three rinses.

steps.title: Perform blank extractions
steps.instruction: For each method (A, BL, BH, C) repeat the entire extraction procedure using the same fluids and equipment but without adding any soil, to generate procedural blanks.

steps.title: Analyze rinses by ion chromatography
steps.instruction: Inject each rinse solution into a Dionex DX‑120 ion chromatograph equipped with AG‑14 and AS‑14 columns, electrolytic suppression, and a sampling loop (25 µL for standard extracts, 200 µL for vadose‑zone samples).

substeps.instruction: Prepare the eluent as a 2.1 mM Na₂CO₃ / 30.8 mM NaHCO₃ buffer made from high‑purity standards.
Inject the filtered rinse sample using the appropriate loop volume.
Quantify chloride using calibration standards: 0.2 mg L⁻¹ (±15 %) and 2.0 mg L⁻¹ (±1.8 %).
Subtract the corresponding procedural blank value from each rinse measurement.

steps.title: Apply modified Method A to vadose‑zone samples
steps.instruction: For 34‑m vadose‑zone borehole material, use Method A with a 1:1 fluid‑to‑soil ratio in duplicate, increase the IC loop to 200 µL, and calculate chloride concentration per dry soil.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize half‑core splits (10 cm diameter) to obtain 50–100 g subsamples.
Add 100 mL deionized water (1:1 ratio) to each 100 g subsample.
Hand‑stir 5 min, shake ~12 h, centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 45 min, and filter supernatant through a Whatman 40 ashless filter; repeat twice for three rinses.
Analyze each rinse by IC using a 200 µL loop as described above.
Sum the blank‑subtracted chloride from the three rinses and divide by the gravimetric water content (see next step) to obtain chloride concentration in vadose‑zone water.

steps.title: Determine gravimetric moisture content
steps.instruction: Measure the water content of the homogenized soil by drying a 400 g sample.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 400 g of homogenized soil.
Dry the sample in an oven at 105 °C for 12 h.
Weigh the dried soil and calculate water content as the weight loss percentage.
